title: Domain tags changed by hand on the tickets screen are overwritten by the next tagging round
story: Adding or removing a domain tag on the tickets screen used to change only the labels, so the next tagging round could overwrite them. Now each change also leaves the hidden tags-by-hand comment, and rounds keep those tags. Removing the last domain now leaves 'no domain' instead of an untagged ticket; removing 'no domain' untags the ticket and hands it back to the tagging round.

checks.criterion: A domain tag added by hand on the tickets screen survives a later tagging round.
checks.steps: Open a made-up test project with a map, two open tickets and members who declared product and platform. Open the tickets screen and open 'Sample ticket 1'. In 'Add a domain…', pick platform. On the map screen, press 'Run tagging round' and wait until the agent goes quiet.
checks.expected: 'Sample ticket 1' still shows only platform, and the other ticket got a domain from the round. In GitHub, 'Sample ticket 1' has a comment starting <!-- grillo:tags-by-hand --> with 'domains: platform'.

checks.criterion: Removing the last domain tag writes the marker with 'no domain'.
checks.steps: On a ticket tagged only platform, press the × on platform.
checks.expected: The tags row shows 'no domain'. In GitHub the ticket carries domain:none, and its newest tags-by-hand comment says 'domains: none'.

checks.criterion: Removing 'no domain' hands the ticket back to the tagging round.
checks.steps: On a ticket tagged 'no domain', press its ×, then run a tagging round.
checks.expected: The ticket shows 'untagged' straight away, and every tags-by-hand comment on it is gone in GitHub. After the round, the ticket has whatever tag the round chose.
